title: Two of six TESS sectors of TIC 300651846 favor profile changes over small shifts
abstract: We test whether small shifts and one depth scale describe the sharp light-curve profile of TIC 300651846. We fit raw TESS samples in six sectors and score separate 6-minute blocks. Each cycle uses a template from all other cycles. A free Fourier shape reduces held-out mean squared error by 8.5 percent in sector 32 and 14.3 percent in sector 64 relative to a template with a shift of up to 0.04 cycles and one scale. Four sectors show no clear gain. A later full-phase shift check retains the two positive gains. Sector 89 also gives an unstable free fit in a rigid control. The main corrected-flux test has 428 cycles. We check aperture flux, background and pointing terms, 8 to 16 Fourier orders and rigid synthetic profiles. These are repeat epochs, not independent telescopes. This result tests a restricted profile model. It does not show material motion, new matter, dust or gas. Correlated noise, flares, template choice and the shift bound limit physical claims. We provide code, derived losses, exact input hashes and separate-scratch retrieval steps. Raw inputs remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Held-out error reduction for a free profile versus a shifted and scaled template. Circles show real observations; crosses show rigid synthetic controls with white noise. Bars are conditional four-cycle block-bootstrap intervals. The second panel shows the cycle at the median corrected-flux gain. The large negative sector 89 value is retained: its synthetic control also has an unstable free fit. Only sectors 32 and 64 have clear positive primary gains.
